claim: HA core's MQTT discovery topic matcher only accepts component/node_id/object_id segments matching [a-zA-Z0-9_-]; any other character makes the topic illegal and HA logs a warning and drops the message.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent discovery publisher must sanitise hostname-derived node/object IDs to [a-zA-Z0-9_-] (e.g. strip dots from FQDNs) or discovery silently fails

claim: HA subscribes to discovery with per-component wildcard topics: <prefix>/<component>/+/config and <prefix>/<component>/+/+/config for every supported component, plus <prefix>/device/+/config and <prefix>/device/+/+/config for device-based discovery.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent can publish either per-entity component discovery or a single device-based discovery message; both subscription paths exist in HA
scope_conditions: HA core dev branch, default discovery prefix homeassistant
quoted_support: for topic in chain((f"{discovery_topic}/{component}/+/config" for component in SUPPORTED_COMPONENTS), (f"{discovery_topic}/{component}/+/+/config" for component in SUPPORTED_COMPONENTS), (f"{discovery_topic}/device/+/config", f"{discovery_topic}/device/+/+/config"))

claim: HA expands MQTT discovery abbreviations (avty_t, cmd_t, stat_t, uniq_id, etc.) before validation, so abbreviated keys in discovery payloads are fully legal first-class syntax.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent can emit compact abbreviated discovery payloads (smaller messages) or full keys; both work
scope_conditions: HA core dev branch; abbreviations from abbreviations.py including DEVICE_ABBREVIATIONS and ORIGIN_ABBREVIATIONS
quoted_support: _replace_all_abbreviations(discovery_payload) ... for key in abbreviations_set.intersection(payload): payload[abbreviations[key]] = payload.pop(key)

claim: The '~' topic-base token in a discovery payload is expanded by HA into every *_topic field (leading or trailing position), including inside availability sub-configs, before entity setup.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent should use ~ topic-base to shorten per-entity discovery payloads across a fleet
quoted_support: def _replace_topic_base(discovery_payload: MQTTDiscoveryPayload) -> None: """Replace topic base in MQTT discovery data.""" base = discovery_payload.pop(TOPIC_BASE) ... if value[0] == TOPIC_BASE and key.endswith("topic"): discovery_payload[key] = f"{base}{value[1:]}"

claim: An EMPTY payload published to a discovery config topic is the official removal semantic: HA cleans up the entity, and for device-based discovery regenerates cleanup messages for every previously discovered component of that device.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent shutdown/uninstall should publish empty discovery payloads (not just rely on LWT) to cleanly remove entities
quoted_support: An empty payload is translated in a cleanup, which forwards an empty payload to all removed components.

claim: HA deduplicates concurrent discovery messages per (component, discovery_id) with a pending deque: if a discovery update arrives while platform setup is still in flight it is queued and replayed, not dropped.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent's republish-on-reconnect storm (birth-message-triggered) will not lose updates even during HA restart races
scope_conditions: HA core dev branch; discovery_pending_discovered structure
quoted_support: if discovery_hash in discovery_pending_discovered: pending = discovery_pending_discovered[discovery_hash]["pending"] pending.appendleft(discovery_payload) ... 'Component has already been discovered: %s %s, queuing update'

claim: HA MQTT discovery does not persist discovery payloads across HA restarts in discovery.py itself — entities surviving an HA restart depend on retained discovery messages or the device re-publishing them (birth-message pattern).
stance_target: ha-linux-agent must publish discovery messages with retain=true and/or republish on HA birth message / broker reconnect to survive HA restarts
scope_conditions: HA core dev branch; in-memory discovery_already_discovered / last_discovery structures

claim: HA supports device-based MQTT discovery where one message on <prefix>/device/<object_id>/config defines the device plus multiple components, each inheriting shared options (availability, command/state topics, encoding, qos) unless overridden at component level.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent should use device-based discovery so one host = one HA device with N entities sharing one availability topic
scope_conditions: HA core dev branch; SHARED_OPTIONS merge
quoted_support: Common options in the body of the device based config are inherited into the component. Unless the option is explicitly specified at component level, in that case the option at component level will override the common option.

claim: Discovery messages carry an origin block (name, sw_version, support_url) that HA logs as 'from external application' — third-party agents like ha-linux-agent are expected to identify themselves in discovery payloads.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent discovery payloads should include an origin block for debuggability and HA-side attribution
